description:
Record a FAILED approach so future agents don't repeat the same mistake.

USE THIS IMMEDIATELY when you try something and it doesn't work. This is the
most valuable type of negative knowledge — it saves hours of debugging for
future agents working on the same codebase.

Auto-validated (no approval cycle). Surfaced FIRST in future get_briefing calls
so it's impossible to miss.

PARAMETERS:
  what       — short title of what you tried (e.g. 'importing X with ESM dynamic import')
  why_failed — the exact error or reason it failed
  instead    — what to do instead (the correct approach)
  scope      — team (default) | personal
  paths      — source files where the issue lives

RETURNS: { id, file_path, action: 'created' }

instead.description: What to use or do instead (recommended alternative)

paths.description: Anchor file paths this applies to

scope.description: Visibility scope. Defaults to personal — EXCEPT when a one-shot `sensor` is attached: an enforced lesson is team truth (the sensor must travel to every machine and CI), so it defaults to team. Pass scope explicitly to override.

sensor.description: ONE-SHOT loop close: validate and attach a sensor in the same call (equivalent to a follow-up propose_sensor). Validated against HEAD — silent on current code, fires on the bad example. If rejected, the attempt is still saved and the verdict tells you how to revise.

absent.description: kind=regex: regex marking CORRECT usage nearby — excludes it from firing

bad_example.description: kind=regex: code snippet the sensor MUST fire on (validation)

command.description: kind=shell|test: command the gate runs when the diff touches the sensor's paths (non-zero exit = lesson fires)

incident.description: Provenance: the incident this sensor guards (e.g. 'prod #442') — surfaced when it fires and in the receipt

kind.description: regex/AST pattern, or a shell/test command

message.description: Self-correction message shown when the sensor fires

pattern.description: kind=regex|ast: pattern matching the faulty usage

red_ref.description: kind=shell|test: pre-fix commit/ref — the oracle must FAIL on it (proves the test catches the incident; records red_proven)

what.description: Brief description of the approach that was tried

why_failed.description: Why it failed or why it should NOT be used

name: mem_tried
